main:2.text: Ellie, Dina, and Shimmer reach the outskirts of Seattle in search of the Washington Liberation Front (WLF). On the way there, Dina guesses why Abby Anderson killed Joel, citing the cannibals and Boston smugglers as possible suspect groups she may have belonged to in the past. Ellie cuts her off, stating that she does not see the point in guessing until they find out more information about Abby and the WLF.

main:3.text: Upon waking up, Ellie soon finds Dina throwing up in a room which houses a radio and a map detailing the different zones the WLF has set up across the city. One of the transmissions details an unknown trespasser causing disturbances in Zone 14, which Dina points out is Hillcrest. Ellie seeks out the trespasser, hoping that it is Tommy.

main:4.text: After recovering from the events in the Lakehill Seattle Hospital, Ellie and Jesse discuss the need to move Dina from the city, as she has come down with a fever. Jesse reveals he has deduced that the symptoms Dina exhibits mean she is pregnant, adding to the urgency to get her home to Jackson. Ellie remains resistant, though, wanting to find Tommy, and also hunt down and kill Abby Anderson.

main:5.text: In April 2034, Abby Anderson runs through a forest searching for her father. She soon finds him, Jerry, who is searching for a zebra he believes is about to give birth. Following tracks, the duo find the zebra caught in a barbed-wire fence. Owen Moore soon joins them, and helps them free the zebra. Once free, Jerry races after it, followed by the others, to find it with its infant.

main:6.text: Manny wakes Abby up at the WLF base in SoundView Stadium. He explains they have been summoned to the Forward operating base (FOB) to meet with the leader, Isaac Dixon. Abby gets up and walks down with him to the canteen, passing the school and gymansium along the way. In the canteen, Manny asks her to collect their food rations while he checks in with his father. While walking to the food line, Abby notices Jordan.

main:7.text: Abby wakes up panicking from a nightmare she had of Lev and Yara dying by the Seraphites' hands because she abandoned them the previous night. She gets dressed, leaves Owen sleeping and hurries back to the coast where she left them at the trailer park. She finds the area is now empty of infected but is instead filled with Seraphites. She fights her way through and reaches the trailer where she left Yara and Lev.

main:8.text: By morning, Abby awakens from a dream. However, unlike her previous dream this one shows her father, peaceful, in the St. Mary's Hospital operating room, where he smiles at her. Abby begins to look around the aquarium, where she is confronted by Mel. Abby attempts to thank her for her help in saving Yara, but Mel berates her, stating she knows Abby still only really cares for herself before storming off.

main:9.text: Several months after the events of Seattle, Ellie is in a farmhouse inspecting Joel's watch. She then hears a baby crying: it is JJ, the son of Jesse and Dina. Ellie picks him up and cheerfully carries him around the house and the outside area. Together they sit on a tractor, admiring a majestic sunset, with Ellie telling him she wants to teach him how to play guitar when he is older.

main:10.text: The chapter opens to Abby and Lev in Santa Barbara. Lev mentions how the two traded one of their guns for information that the Fireflies are stationed at 2425 Constance, which is found on the street that they are on. Lev is doubtful but Abby asks him to try being more upbeat, suggesting they head down the street to find the house. On the way, they encounter a small group of runners but kill them.

main:11.text: Ellie stands outside the farm, her two missing fingers now stitched up and once again wearing Dina's lucky charm bracelet. She walks up to the house, finding it decaying from the outside and the fields deserted of the sheep and hay that once filled them. She enters the house, finding it just as bare as outside. It is clear Dina and JJ have not lived here in some time.

collectible:1.text: Trading cards are a category of collectibles found in The Last of Us Part II and are only collected by Ellie. They appear as trading cards of a fictional collectible card game known as Society of Champions. The trading cards are a part of the same fictional franchise as the Savage Starlight comics found in The Last of Us, as a card can be found featuring the comic's protagonist, Dr. Daniela Star.

main:1.text: The scene opens with Ellie drinking privately in an alley outside of the party. Once she finishes her drink, she proceeds to the courtyard area where many people are gathered, drinking, conversing and celebrating. She wanders around, talking to the various people, taking part in the games and even playing a game of Get the Clicker with some of the children.

collectible:2.text: Coins are a category of collectibles found in The Last of Us Part II and are only collected by Abby Anderson. Coins are US 50 State quarters which feature a portrait of George Washington on the obverse and a unique designs for each of the 50 US states on the reverse. There are a total of 32 coins that can be found in the game. Each coin is unique, as the quarter for a given state is only found once.

collectible:3.text: Artifacts are one of the four categories of collectible that appear in The Last of Us on PS3 and its Remastered edition on the PS4. They are also the only category of collectibles obtained in the associated DLC, Left Behind. Artifacts return as one of four collectible categories in The Last of Us Part II.

collectible:4.text: Ellie's journal is an artifact that is found during the "Jackson" chapter in The Last of Us Part II. It is an old journal owned by Ellie. Here she draws and writes her thoughts throughout the game. Ellie's journal can be found in her house on a desk close to her jacket. It is automatically picked up when she leaves to go on patrol with Dina.

collectible:5.text: Safes are item caches that can be found in the The Last of Us and The Last of Us Part II. They contain supplies abandoned by people during the initial outbreak or stashed during later conflicts. They require a combination to open, which can be found on certain Artifacts or in the environment. Safes can hold ammo, crafting supplies, parts, and even Training Manuals.

collectible:6.text: A workbench is used in The Last of Us and in The Last of Us Part II to upgrade firearms to make them more powerful. To upgrade them, parts are needed, as well as tools upgrades in the first game. As Joel acquires weapons, tools, and parts, he can use them to make his weapons more powerful, such as faster reloading and adding a second gun holsters.

easter-egg:1.text: The antique ring found in Ellie's Seattle Day 1 chapter is Francis Drake's ring from the Uncharted series.

easter-egg:2.text: The strange relic found by Abby in her Seattle Day 1 chapter is a reference to the Precursor orb from the Jak and Daxter series. The Precursor orb also appears as an artifact of the same name in the Uncharted series.

easter-egg:3.text: Photos of Naughty Dog staff members' pets are seen in the game, such as sound implementer Christopher Walasek's cat appearing on "missing cat" posters around Seattle, and game designer Pete Ellis's cat Reginald, who appears on a calendar in Ellie's Seattle Day 2 chapter.
